Root cause: apply_focus's fit_radius_for_view only considered the focused component's own AABB, so a tiny target (e.g. two ions) deep inside a much larger rendered structure pulled the camera in close enough to near-clip through the surrounding geometry. Fix: added Ctx.scene_bounds, accumulated as the union of every rendered component's world-space AABB (render_representation); apply_focus now takes max(fit_radius_for_view(focus_aabb), fit_radius_for_view_from_center(focus_center, scene_aabb)) via a new fit_radius_for_view_from_center helper (refactored out of fit_radius_for_view). When focus==scene (the common whole-structure case) the two radii coincide, so ferritin-ala.5's tight single-structure fit is unaffected -- confirmed by all existing focus tests still passing. New test test_focus_small_target_clamped_to_scene_bounds proves the same tiny target's radius is >3x larger when a full structure is also rendered around it vs. focused in isolation. 109 tests pass. Root cause: fit_radius_for_view_from_center used the vertical half-FOV (22.5deg) for BOTH axes, over-estimating the distance needed to fit the horizontal extent on a widescreen viewport (true horizontal FOV is wider). Fix: query the live camera's logical_viewport_size() in execute_mvs_on_load, compute aspect_ratio, thread it through Ctx to fit_radius_for_view/fit_radius_for_view_from_center, and derive the horizontal half-FOV via atan(aspect*tan(v_half_fov)) instead of reusing the vertical one. When the vertical extent is already the binding constraint (common for roughly-square/tall structures, e.g. preset_symmetry), the fix is a no-op by design -- confirmed via test_fit_radius_unaffected_by_aspect_for_tall_aabb. For horizontally-dominant AABBs the radius now shrinks (test_fit_radius_tighter_on_widescreen_for_wide_aabb). 111 tests pass. Visually re-confirmed via fresh capture: preset_label now shows the full structure comfortably framed (previously two giant magenta ion spheres filled the frame with backbone near-clipping -- see t0h.5, fixed together) and preset_superposition frames both copies without clipping.

Root cause: the cartoon ribbon's cross-section frame was purely parallel-transported from an arbitrary seed (tangent x global-Y at the first point), with no relation to the actual backbone geometry -- so the flat sheet ellipse's orientation didn't track any meaningful anatomical direction, making it read as a round-ish tube from most camera angles rather than a recognizable flat ribbon. Fix: added peptide_plane_normals (Carson-Bugg virtual-torsion construction: normalize((CA[i]-CA[i-1]) x (CA[i+1]-CA[i])), sign-corrected across residues to avoid the 180-degree flip that occurs roughly every residue in extended/beta conformations), interpolated onto the finer curve via nlerp_direction, and a new sweep_frames_oriented that steers each ring's up vector toward this per-point hint (projected perpendicular to the tangent) instead of blind parallel transport -- falling back to parallel transport when the hint is degenerate (parallel to tangent) and sign-correcting against the previous frame so rings still can't flip 180 degrees (preserves the t0h.2 no-spikes property). Applied only to Cartoon (render_cartoon_mapped); Putty's circular cross-section has no orientation to get wrong, so it keeps plain sweep_frames. New tests: test_peptide_plane_normals_sign_corrected_and_unit, test_sweep_frames_oriented_tracks_hint_and_stays_continuous, test_sweep_frames_oriented_falls_back_when_hint_degenerate. 114 tests pass. Visually re-confirmed via fresh capture: no regression on 4hhb (still smooth, correctly colored/segmented, no new artifacts) -- but 4hhb is almost all helix with negligible sheet content, so the flat-ribbon orientation improvement itself couldn't be visually confirmed against real sheet geometry with the test data available this session; the underlying mechanism is verified by the three unit tests instead.

Root cause: bond cylinders were a single mesh whose every vertex mapped to atom_a in atom_map (render_ballandstick_mapped) or was baked with a flat grey color (render_ballandstick), so the MVS color theme (which recolors every vertex by its atom_map entry) painted the whole stick as atom_a's element color -- the second endpoint's color never appeared. Fix: added Structure::half_bond_cylinders(pos1, pos2, radius), splitting a bond into two half-length cylinders at its midpoint. render_ballandstick_mapped now maps the first half's vertices to idx_a and the second half's to idx_b; render_ballandstick (the non-MVS baked-color path) now colors each half by its own endpoint atom's element color via self.color_scheme. New tests: test_half_bond_cylinders_splits_at_midpoint (geometric: verifies each half's vertex positions stay within its half of the bond span), test_half_bond_cylinders_degenerate_returns_none, and test_ballandstick_bond_second_endpoint_gets_own_atom_map_entries (finds a real atom that is only ever a bond's second endpoint in protein_01 and proves its atom_map count now exceeds its own sphere's vertex count, i.e. it receives bond contributions instead of zero). 117 tests pass. Visually re-captured: no regression on rep_BallAndStick_ElementSymbol (structure renders correctly); the two-tone effect itself is subtle at whole-structure zoom and best seen zoomed into an individual bond, which wasn't practical to capture this session, so it's verified via the dedicated unit tests instead.

Line representation was a GPU LineList (hard 1px, no normals, no AA) — replaced with thin triangle cylinders (LINE_RADIUS=0.13 Å, via existing half_bond_cylinders helper, split at midpoint per endpoint atom like BallAndStick bonds). Now has real normals so it's lit and anti-aliased instead of aliasing to hairline on large structures (verified on 4hhb via bevy_capture_representations). Removed the now-unnecessary unlit-material special-case in mvs_executor.rs for Wireframe. 117 tests pass (topology assertion updated LineList->TriangleList, unlit test flipped to lit).

The legacy pre-1.6 container is a 2020-era artifact. ProtBert is the sole survivor of it in this space, and it is superseded by ESM-2, ProtT5, Ankh and ESM-C. Writing a legacy-pickle deserializer to reach one obsolete model is not worth the maintenance surface.

IMPORTANT DISTINCTION worth keeping: zip-format pickle is NOT a problem — candle's PthTensors reads it, and most good protein LMs (including most of ferritin's working registry) ship it. Only the legacy container is unreadable. A blanket 'no pickle' rule would delete ESM-1v, ESM-1b, SaProt, ESMC-300M/600M and ESM3 from the registry.

WON'T DO — ProtBert is superseded and unloadable.

Two independent reasons, both established by measurement rather than judgement:

1. FORMAT. Rostlab/prot_bert and prot_bert_bfd ship the legacy pre-torch-1.6 pickle container. candle's PthTensors is zip-only and rejects them ('invalid Zip archive: Could not find EOCD', confirmed by running it against the real 1.68 GB file). A 20-model survey found ProtBert is the ONLY legacy-format protein LM in the space, so the reader that would fix it (ferritin-goh.10) is closed as won't-do.

2. SUPERSEDED. ProtBert is 2020. It is displaced by ESM-2, ProtT5, Ankh and ESM-C, all of which ferritin either has or can reach.

PR #198 implemented the tokenizer and config mapping and was closed unmerged; the branch feat/protbert-tokenizer is kept if this is ever revisited.

WHAT THE WORK ESTABLISHED, worth keeping:
- candle's bert::Config cannot deserialize Rostlab's config.json — it omits layer_norm_eps, pad_token_id and model_type. Anyone wiring a BERT-family protein model through candle-transformers hits this.
- TokenizerSpec::HfVocabTxt is in practice a proxy for 'SaProt': both esm2_runner.rs and tests/test_conformance.rs branch on it, the latter to build SaProt's two-character M#Q#I#... alphabet. Only one vocab.txt model remains, so this is latent, not live — but the next vocab.txt model over a different alphabet will be fed SaProt's sequence and asserted on. Filed separately.

THE GOAL THIS ISSUE ACTUALLY SERVED — proving TokenizerSpec owns input preprocessing rather than leaking it into caller code — is now unmet and needs another vehicle. ProstT5 (ferritin-goh.6) is the natural candidate: it needs whitespace-separated residues, which is the same contract test ProtBert was chosen for.
